lines.narration: Off the line the two cars come side by side, and Sean's black-and-white Mustang grinds door to door with DK's coupe in a long shower of orange sparks. By the next bend the rival's flank is torn open and he is fighting the wheel to stay straight.
Sean drags up level out of a near-black frame, headlights blazing, and carves past DK out of a smoke-filled cliff-edge turn. For one corner the kid who got laughed out of every garage is in front.

DK will not have it. He snarls at the wheel and drives his coupe straight into the Mustang's flank mid-drift, scraping the two of them along the cliff edge until Sean breaks free and carves the next corner alone.

claim.subject: the heavyset driver in the white tank top

lines.narration: They come down the road door to door, trading paint, each trying to force the other wide, and neither gives. Then DK edges back in front and hauls across the lane to crowd Sean off the road.

claim.subject: the heavyset driver in the white tank top

lines.narration: This is the mountain only DK has ever reached the bottom of, and he is driving like it. A guardrail bend comes up fast and he leans out over his wheel, muscling the Mustang toward the edge. One of them is about to run out of road.

claim.subject: the driver in the white tank top

lines.narration: And Sean does the one thing DK never saw coming. Instead of giving the edge up, he shoves back, putting the coupe off the shoulder into the brush, and the mountain's only master goes tumbling across the dirt. The gaijin they all mocked just ran DK's road and left DK in the weeds.
Sean coasts to a stop and the whole crowd breaks off the barrier and sprints the road to swarm his window, while the wrecked car lies upside down and smoking behind them.
Neela reaches him through the noise, and the strained look he has been holding all the way down the mountain finally breaks into a grin as their friends crowd in around them.
Then three men in black walk up out of the dark, one of them under Kamata's wide-brimmed hat, and the celebration stops dead in front of them.

claim.subject: the older man in the black hat and long coat

lines.narration: Kamata says his piece straight at Sean, who takes it with his eyes lowered. There is no threat left in it. The old man's own face sags, then he drops his head and turns away from the crowd - the race was the hearing, and his nephew lost it.

claim.subject: the older man in the black hat and long coat

lines.narration: Cut to a packed night garage meet. Money comes out, and Twinkie works through the crowd collecting fistfuls of cash as the bets on Sean are settled.

claim.subject: the young man in the green jacket and white do-rag

lines.narration: Here is what the win actually bought. Sean stands in DK's place now, his crew taking the house cut from the same crowd that once mocked him - and Twinkie calls him out across the garage, telling him Han was family. Sean's smirk fades, and the woman in the red top holds his eye while he hears it.

claim.subject: the young man in the green jacket and white do-rag

lines.narration: He leaves the crowd for the driver's seat, hands on the wheel, watching his garage through the glass. The mountain is his now, and so is the next race - he lines up in it himself.

And the car that noses up beside him is no tuner coupe - it's a hulking American muscle car, and the camera pushes in on a bald man in a white tee at the wheel. A stranger. A racer who knew Han, come all the way from America to take on the new king of this mountain.

claim.subject: the bald man in the white tee

lines.narration: They size each other up through the windows, and the wariness thaws - the bald man laughing, Sean grinning back. Then comes the warning that doubles as the film's last word: this ain't no ten-second race.

claim.subject: the bald man in the white tee

lines.narration: Sean spent his whole life being moved on - new town, new school, new nobody - and he only wins the day he stops running and plants his feet on the one road everyone said he had no business on. A woman in red walks out between the cars, both engines light their tyres, she throws her arms up, and the film cuts to black mid-launch. If that landed for you, tell me what to recap next, and I'll meet you at the start line.
